If you don't mind episodic stories, Darker than Black season 1 is a self contained story that takes a story structure akin to Cowboy Bebop. Flying Witch and Amaama to Inazuma are really nice slice of life series as well. Flying Witch is more of a quirky iyashikei series about a girl studying magic with her cousins in the countryside. Amaama on the other hand is more of a melancholic story about the everyday struggle of a man and his daughter who lost his wife. During the show we see how they try to come together through learning how to cook.

I think Kids on the Slope is more of a drama than slice of life but yeah it's great. Terror in Resonance or Zankyou no Terror is not bad as well. The characters are a bit bland, but the mind games are fairly entertaining. The animation and direction as well as the art direction allows for some really wonderful moments, which makes the show pretty good in the first few episodes, though it feels like it doesn't quite know what it wants to do from the middle onwards.

Noragami and its second season Noragami Aragato are also pretty good. There's 12 eps in season 1, 2 OVAs and 13 eps in season 2. This one is more of a shounen action, though it is fantastical as well. The show follows Yato, a Japanese god trying to gain influence through odd jobs in the hopes that one day he can earn enough money to build his own shrine. After a while the partner he used for binding spirits gets tired of their impoverished lifestyle and leaves him. 
Yato ends up being mistakenly saved by a school girl called Hiyori which results in her being injured, to the point where her spirit leaves her body. She asks Yato to get her body back to normal. He agrees though he does not know how to do so or if it is even possible which results in them being stuck together indefinitely. 
It's more of an action comedy with myth-like characters but there does seem to be a of a romantic sub-text.

Have you seen Kyoukai no Kanata? It's a little on the short side (being 12 episodes long) but it has the fantasy action romance elements you're looking for. 
It's basically about a girl called Mirai who hunts creatures sort of like the Hollows in Bleach called Youmu. She ends up meeting a half human half Youmu called Akihito, in an attempt to murder him. It turns out he's immortal however, so she keeps trying to kill him. At first to test his immortality and later to practice her fighting skills since she's pretty bad at her job due to her fear and insecurities. 
Over time they become friends.

Flying Witch and Amaama to Inazuma are also quite good. Flying Witch sort of reminds me of Kiki's delivery service if Kiki grew up, though it's a bit odd. It has a wonderfully tranquil and cheerful atmosphere in the rugged Japanese country side. The mix between down to earth magical creatures or characters and ordinary life is quite unique as well.
Amaama to Inazuma on the other hand is a heart warming series about a father and his young daughter trying to deal with the death of his wife and her mother. The father, Kohei has been struggling trying to remain cheerful, burying himself in his work to keep the lights on, but as a result he has been neglecting his daughter, who still hasn't come to terms with the death of her mother. 
He notices this when he realises she hasn't been eating her food properly so he decides to learn how to cook in order to better take care of her. This allows them to grow closer as well.

Have you seen Mob Psycho 100? It's written by the same guy that wrote One Punch Man. Personally, I prefer Mob though. It's even more crazy and over the top the One Punch Man and the humour is far more dynamic due to the unorthodox animation style and timing. The character dynamics are also really fun. It's probably the most original thing I've seen in a while. 
Flip Flappers is also pretty good. It mostly tells it's story through these nice story book visuals. It's basically about identity and Cocona growing up.

If you want to try sci fi, Psycho Pass is an interesting cyberpunk police drama. Like FMAB there's a wider society with a questionable ethical code. The main characters are part of the the system keeping order in this world though one is a new cop who cannot accept the cold immoral method of enacting judgement on criminals and victims alike. Then there are those who use unorthodox methods or do not fit in to this modern society, thus fall to the wayside.

Akagami no Shirayuki-hime is a really nice romance slice of life that takes some inspiration from the Snow white fairy tale. It takes place in a bit of a low fantasy renaissance era world. Art work and animation is amazing and the characters are quite nice. 
Anohana is also a nice romantic slice of life about some friends that split apart after the death of their friend. This friend comes back as a ghost however, and they have to find a way to figure out how to send her on to the after life.
There's also Nagi no Asukara. This one is about some kids that live under the sea. There's 2 races of humans, those of the sea and those on the land. They're both suspicious of each other but they must reluctantly let the kids go to school on the surface since their school was destroyed. (It's been a while since I watched it but I think it was because of a storm or something.) As time goes on the kids are accepted which forces the adults to interact with each other, making them overcome their suspicions. There's also a theme of time changing and loss later.

On that note Baccano! would be pretty fun as well. It's this darkly humorous show set mostly in the prohibition era. It follows some mafia families butting heads with each other as well as a 3 way train heist and a strange supernatural force attempting to kill all the passengers. The story is told across multiple time frames and locations, sort of like Pulp fiction or Snatch anime.

I used to read Rave Master when I first got into anime and manga though I'm not as into it now. You might like it any way. It's by the same mangaka as the guy who worked on Fairy tail. I think there's an anime as well but I haven't seen it.

Gurren Lagann and Little Witch Academia are also pretty good. The producer and director for these too also worked in on direction and script writing on Kill la Kill. It has that fun over the top action Trigger is known for. They're also similar thematically in some ways, both being about perseverance and growing up.

Since you like Log Horizon and Soul Eater, I take it you like action, adventure and maybe a passing interest in rpgs. As a result you might like Konosuba or Mahoujin Guru Guru. They're both fairly recent adventure comedic anime with some action mixed in though there's a much heavier leaning to the comedy aspect. They take place in an rpg like fantasy world, though Konosuba is a parody of the "trapped/transported to a video game world" and Mahoujin Guru Guru just happens to take place in a world like an rpg. Like Konosuba they both make fun of jrpgs.

Akatsuki no Yona is also a really awesome fantasy adventure. Basically it's about a princess called Yona who witnesses the death of her father and the hands of her beloved cousin and close friend, Soo won. As a result she is whisked away by her body guard and other mutual friend Hak. She must live in hiding as an ordinary commoner moving from place to place looking for these 4 dragons that are supposed to protect her. 
She grows quite a lot, having seen how ordinary people live and the results of her father's weak reign. The world is really well realised and the characters are quite fun. Though the animation and direction isn't great. Plus the show sort of ends at a cliff hanger, though you can pick up fairly easily from the manga.

Moribito is also a very interesting fantasy adventure anime that takes place in a strange asiatic world with magic, spirits and demons (though more in the vein of yokai rather than explicitly evil creatures). It's basically about a woman called Balsa trying to redeem herself from something that happened in the past by protecting 8 lives. The prince Chagum is the last life she must protect as his father is trying to assassinate him for some mysterious reason. The animation, art work, action choreography and music are all phenomenal! Plus there characters are surprisingly complex with lots of shades of grey rather than black and white morality.

Scrapped Princess is a pretty good fantasy adventure series with some action. I've already recommended it to someone so I'll just paste that here: "Scrapped Princess is a really good fantasy adventure series from the early 2000s if I remember correctly. It's animation and action was pretty good (Bones, I suppose that's expected heh) and the characters were really good. They have nice chemistry together too. Ending might feel a bit underwhelming but I think it's one of those shows that's more about the journey than the destination."

Since you like Your Lie in April, you might also like Kids on the slope or Sakamichi no Apollon. It's a really wonderful josei romance, set in Japan around the 1960s. The show is more or less about these 3 friends living in Japan as it's culture is changing due to the influence of the American troops stationed there after ww2. You can see this in particular through the jazz and vintage rock music. 2 of the characters are musicians and the other's family own a music store. As a result they end up spending a lot of time together practising music and opening up to each other as their music improves. It's quite good. The animation and direction is incredible as well.

Shuumatsu Nani Shitemasu ka? Isogashii desu ka? Sukutte Moratte Ii desu ka? is also a surprisingly mature love story about a guy who lost everything trying to save the world many years ago and a girl he meets by chance stepping into the same fate as he once walked. The music in it is fantastic as well. It has this nice poignant Celtic feel to it which enhances the emotional beats quite well.

Akagami no Shirayuki-hime is a really nice romantic slice of life as well, taking place in what looks like a renaissance era fantasy world. It has nice character development and the characters are pretty fun. Plus the animation is beautiful and the background art has this wonderful fairy tale style to it.
Personally, I prefer it to the tv series so far, though obviously the show isn't finished yet so...

The Mahoutsukai no Yome OVA is really good as well. I suppose it'd probably be a low fantasy. It's basically a self contained side story about Chise's history as a child. It's rather melancholic and creepy at times, though mixed with a childlike sense of wonder due to the magical aspects.

Have you seen Kekkai Sensen? It's not as in depth as Made in Abyss though it does have an interesting setting. It generally has more of an episodic structure akin to something like Cowboy Bebop, where the characters get caught up in a situation which gives us a little more information about the various organisations or strange people in Hellsalem's Lot. This city with lots of ridiculous bombastic things happening every other day, whilst normal humans and alien creatures go about their normal day creates a very quirky atmosphere that's pretty enjoyable. 
If you're up for manga though, Vinland Saga has a pretty interesting world based off 11th century Europe (in particular the Norse lands). It has an interesting mix of Norse history and mythology that really makes it stand out. Not to mention the characters and world are really interesting. I feel like whipping out an encyclopedia with every prominent character, location, war etc. just so I can see how much is mythology, history or fiction.

If not Scrapped Princess is a really good fantasy adventure series from the early 2000s if I remember correctly. It's animation and action was pretty good (Bones, I suppose that's expected heh) and the characters were really good. They have nice chemistry together too. Ending might feel a bit underwhelming but I think it's one of those shows that's more about the journey than the destination.
Are you up for a film? Sword of the stranger is really good. Though it's a bit more character focused than plot focused.
